purpose: Corollary 1 of the KDA paper classifies write rules by which receipt class transports a boundary receipt exactly when the suffix inputs are held fixed: additive writes keep a static receipt, per-channel (or per-head) decay needs only a diagonal ledger, and a delta rule (diagonal minus rank-one transition) needs the full matrix product. Native forcing (changed suffix inputs when the record is omitted) is predicted nonzero for every multi-layer model. These predictions were recorded before any family other than Kimi KDA and Qwen3.5 GDN was run.

mamba2.transition: S_t = exp(dt_t A_h) S_{t-1} + dt_t x_t B_t^T, one scalar per head
mamba2.expectation_note: Single recurrent channel and no attention rows: any recovery of the secret must come from the recurrent residual, so probe lift after full transport should fall with the residual rather than stay at the record-present level as it does in the Kimi hybrid.

falcon_h1.transition: Mamba-2 mixer in parallel with softmax attention in every layer
falcon_h1.expectation_note: Attention rows carry the record as in Kimi; recurrent corrections alone should leave the probe near the record-present level.

rwkv7.transition: S_t = (diag(exp(w_t)) - (kk_t * a_t) kk_t^T) S_{t-1} + k_t v_t^T
rwkv7.expectation_note: Single recurrent channel with a delta-class transition: the diagonal ledger should fail even under frozen inputs, and probe recovery should track the recurrent residual.

kda.status: measured in kimi_sv.eval_forcing_sweep and the published transport audit
